name: PT Indah Kiat Pulp & Paper Tbk

frontmatter.title: Indah Kiat Pulp & Paper: a trough-cycle board and pulp producer priced for the group, not the mill
frontmatter.summary: INKP trades at a fraction of the value of four Indonesian pulp and paper mills whose capex has just peaked. At the last actual's economics and a through-cycle margin, DCF value is far above the price; the Sinar Mas ownership discount explains much of the gap and closes only slowly.
thesis: The market prices INKP at 0.3x book and 4.3x last year's earnings, the arithmetic of a mill complex expected to earn nothing through the cycle, while the last actual year earned a 32.2% gross margin at trough product prices and the forecast normalises no higher than that.
Capex peaked with the Karawang containerboard mill: 25.1% of sales in FY2025 falling to 10.0% by FY2030E. That single line converts an unexciting earnings stream into US$521.3m of free cash flow.
Our through-cycle DCF gives Rp14,623 a share; the Sinar Mas konglo lens, which keeps only part of any gap within twelve months, sets the target at Rp10,086 (57.9%).

The bear is a cash-cycle bear, not only a price bear: the 2026 trough margin persists, capex does not normalise, and a quarter of the related-party receivable book is never collected - a Rp6,660 outcome, barely above today's price.
Governance is the swing factor: a 58.3% controller, a token dividend (5.0% payout) and receivables worth nearly half of sales. We would not own this for the dividend; we own it for the asset.

catalysts.event: First IDX minimum-free-float step for large caps; INKP is already compliant at {{mkt.free_float_pct|pctv}}, so no forced selling
MSCI decision on moving Indonesia to Standalone status, which would remove the residual index bid for large IDX names
FY2026 audited results: first full year with the Karawang mill and the twenty-year tax holiday in the tax line
Q4-2026 results - watch gross margin for the first evidence that Karawang startup costs are behind the mill

blocks.text: **BUY**, target **Rp10,086**, price Rp6,425, expected return 57.9%. The target is not a view on the pulp price. It is what four Indonesian mills with US$3,171.3m of sales and US$796.7m of recent capital spending are worth at the margin the last actual year actually earned, carried forward at a house cost of capital of 10.4%, and then discounted for the fact that the controlling family decides when that value is recognised.

The variant view has three parts. First, the market is valuing the equity at 0.3x of book and 4.3x of last year's earnings - the arithmetic of a business expected to lose money through a cycle, not one that earned an EBITDA margin of 29.3% of sales in FY2024, restated from the LK, and 21.3% in FY2025A on the data pack basis - the one year our LK set does not let us restate, as the financials section explains. Second, the capex cycle has turned: 25.1% of sales in FY2025 was the Karawang build, and the run-rate is already 17.0% in our FY2026E, falling to 10.0% - the difference between a company that consumes cash and one that returns it. Third, the ownership discount is real but bounded: a 58.3% controller, no index-membership risk (INKP is not on the exchange's high-concentration list and its float of 39.7% clears the new minimum), and a lens that closes only 30.0% of the price-to-value gap in our base case.

The price is 43.7% of fundamental value today: Rp6,425 against Rp14,704. The fundamental value we carry twelve months out is Rp17,645, and the konglo lens turns that into Rp10,086; the base regime scenario closes 30.0% of the log gap, the bear scenario assumes the discount widens into a market-wide de-rating, the bull scenario closes most of it.

What would change our mind, in order of importance: a gross margin that stays below thirty per cent for two more quarters (the Karawang ramp is not a ramp but a permanently worse cost position); an equity raise or a related-party asset purchase that moves cash out of the minority's reach; and a pulp price collapse that takes the through-cycle margin with it. None of these is in the base case, and each is priced in the risk section.

PT Indah Kiat Pulp & Paper Tbk was founded in 1976 and has been listed on the Jakarta exchange since 1990; it is a Sinar Mas (Widjaja family) vehicle whose immediate parent is PT APP Purinusa Ekapersada [S4]. It runs four production sites - Perawang in Riau, Tangerang, Serang in Banten and Karawang - and produces pulp, cultural paper (coated and uncoated writing and printing paper), tissue and industrial paper, principally containerboard (linerboard and corrugated medium), boxboard, food packaging and converted corrugated containers [S4].

The business model is vertical integration around a fibre base. Pulp from Perawang feeds the paper machines, paper feeds the converting lines, and the group's plantation and chip supply sits above it. That integration is why INKP's margins have historically been wider than a standalone converter's, and it is also why the company is exposed to two prices at once - pulp and containerboard - rather than one. The company does not publish a segment split in the material we could retrieve, so we do not claim one: revenue is US$3,171.3m and the mix between pulp, cultural paper, tissue and industrial paper sits in the annual report's management discussion, not in a form we could verify line by line [S3].

The customer base is export-weighted. The group sells into Asia, the United States, Australia, the Middle East, Africa and Europe [S0], and Indonesia's pulp and paper industry exported US$8.2 billion in 2025 [S2]. For INKP specifically the export share is not disclosed in the documents we hold; what is disclosed is a receivables book of a size that suggests a concentrated, partly related-party customer base (see the financial section).

Strategy is capacity-led and downstream. The fourth mill at Karawang adds industrial paper capacity and is the reason capex ran at 40.1% of sales in FY2024; the company has secured a twenty-year tax holiday around the fourth mill's operation [S8]. Management's stated direction - more industrial paper, less dependence on pulp price volatility - is the right one for a producer whose pulp exposure produced both its best year (FY2022A, gross margin 39.7%) and its worst (FY2025A, 32.2%).

Position in the industry: INKP is one of the two large integrated Indonesian producers alongside its Sinar Mas sister PT Pabrik Kertas Tjiwi Kimia, and the group is the country's largest pulp and paper complex. We treat "largest" as background rather than a sourced share: the industry association publishes national capacity and output, not company shares [S2].

Ownership and control: PT APP Purinusa Ekapersada holds 58.3%; the public holds 41.7%, of which the exchange registry counts 39.7% as free float (house konglo registry, as of 27 October 2026; the annual report shows only the two stakes above) [S5]. There is no dual-class structure and no evidence of pledged controller shares in the documents we retrieved - which is not the same as proof that none exist; we could not obtain a pledge disclosure for the parent.

Indonesia is a globally relevant pulp and paper producer, and a structurally low-cost one: tropical hardwood plantations close to the mills, integrated power, and a large domestic packaging market. The Ministry of Industry's data, presented at the APKI congress in November 2026, put national pulp production at 11.7 million tonnes in 2025 against installed capacity of 14.5 million tonnes a year - utilisation of roughly four-fifths - and exports of US$8.2 billion [S2]. The same source notes that paper capacity exceeds paper output by a similar margin and that government policy is focused on downstream packaging, tissue and rayon fibre, plus recycling-chain and decarbonisation support [S2].

The cycle is the whole story for a name like this. FY2022A gross margin of 39.7% was a pulp and board price peak; FY2025A's 32.2% is the same assets at a trough. Revenue fell from US$4,002.6m to US$3,171.3m on price, not tonnage [S3]. That is the definition of a price-taker, and it is why the house method for this industry values the assets through the cycle rather than at a spot margin.

**The through-cycle anchor.** We could not archive a public pulp or containerboard price series: the industry source gives national volumes and values, not a per-tonne price [S2], and the issuer does not disclose tonnage. We therefore express the through-cycle price through the one series the LK does publish - the realised gross margin - and set the base at 31.5%, below every year in the FY2022-FY2025 range and below its four-year average, so the base does not require a price recovery. The bull lifts the margin to that four-year average; the bear takes it to the Q3-2026 trough. NAV at spot prices is the base DCF of Rp14,623; the through-cycle case is the same assets at the four-year average margin, which is the bull scenario at Rp24,006 today and Rp28,827 on the twelve-month basis used in the scenario table. We do not claim a cost-curve quartile: no cost-curve study is in the archive, and the qualitative claim - tropical hardwood fibre next to the mill, integrated power - is background, not a sourced rank [S2, S4].

Demand drivers: global containerboard consumption tracks e-commerce and goods trade; tissue tracks urbanisation and income; cultural paper is in structural decline in the developed world and still growing in South and Southeast Asia. Supply drivers: Indonesian and Brazilian hardwood pulp capacity additions, which arrive two to four years after price peaks [S2]. The industry's own utilisation numbers - capacity about a quarter above output - say that the marginal tonne is not scarce, which caps the through-cycle margin rather than the spot one.

Regulation that matters to INKP: forestry and land-use compliance (the group's fibre supply is the largest single ESG exposure), export-proceeds retention rules that affect how export dollars are held, and the tax regime. The twenty-year tax holiday around the fourth mill [S8] is mill-specific and time-limited, so it explains only part of why the effective rate the LK shows sits below the statutory rate; the rest is ordinary permanent differences, and we revert the terminal year to the rate the LK actually paid in FY2024 rather than capitalise the holiday in perpetuity.

Competitive position and moat. The moat is the fibre base and the scale of the mill complex, not a brand or a patent. A new entrant cannot replicate a plantation licence, a twenty-five-year asset base and a port in Riau at a cost that beats the incumbent. Against that, the moat does not protect the margin: every producer in the basin gets the same price, and INKP's cost position is good but not unique. Five forces, honestly: supplier power is low (own fibre, contracted wood), buyer power is high (global commodity buyers, thin differentiation), new entry is low (permits, capital, fibre), substitutes are moderate (plastic in packaging, digital in cultural paper), and rivalry is high and rising as Indonesian and Brazilian capacity comes on. That is a "good asset, cyclical price" industry, not a franchise [S2, S4].

**Revenue.** FY2022A US$4,002.6m, FY2023A US$3,479.0m, FY2024A US$3,195.7m, FY2025A US$3,171.3m - a price-led decline of -13.1%, -8.1% and -0.8% as the pulp cycle deflated [S3]. The nine months to September 2026 already show the turn: net sales grew by double digits year on year as the Karawang mill added volume [S0]. We forecast 11.1% for FY2026E - the run-rate, not a forecast of a price recovery - then 3.0% volume-led growth tapering to a 2.0% terminal [S3].

**Margins.** Gross margin 39.7% → 32.5% → 31.9% → 32.2%, and 30.0% in our base case. The FY2026E number is not a haircut invented for safety: the nine months to September ran near that level with Q3 below thirty per cent, as the new mill carried pre-commercial startup costs into cost of sales [S0]. From FY2027E we return to 31.0% and then 31.5%, still below the FY2025A actual, because the mix shifts toward industrial paper as Karawang ramps. Operating costs are held at the last actual: SG&A US$351.8m in FY2025A, US$391.1m in FY2026E, the same share of sales [S6].

**The D&A restatement - read this before the EBITDA line.** The data pack's depreciation charge is unusable: US$7.5m against a fixed-asset base that runs on US$796.7m of annual capex and a twenty-five-year machinery life [S7]. For the two years the LK lets us rebuild we have restated it: FY2024A D&A of US$283.5m and FY2023A of US$226.8m, both taken from the issuer's own ratio table - EBITDA of 29.3% of net sales in FY2024 and 29.2% in FY2023, less the reported operating profit for each year [S6] - so the history now carries the 29.3% FY2024 EBITDA margin the issuer discloses rather than the pack's understated figure. The audited cash-flow note independently gives US$252.9m for FY2022 [S7], and the depreciation policy on a net asset base of several billion dollars is consistent with the restated charge [S7]. We model D&A at a fixed share of revenue - US$274.8m in FY2026E - and every forecast EBITDA figure in this report is on that basis. One limitation is recorded in the fact file rather than papered over: the FY2025 documents we hold give revenue and operating profit but no depreciation note, so FY2025A EBITDA of US$675.2m stays on the pack basis. That is the only year in the history not restated, and no valuation leg uses it: the EV/EBITDA cross-check was removed rather than applied to an understated metric.

**Cash flow and working capital.** Operating cash flow covered capex only barely in FY2025A (FCFF US$206.1m on US$796.7m of capex) - the mill was being built. The working-capital intensity is the other unusual feature: operating working capital of US$2,256.0m on sales of US$3,171.3m, driven by receivables (the LK's receivable balance is close to half of annual sales) rather than inventory [S6]. We hold that ratio at 71.0% of sales - receivables plus inventory plus advances less trade payables, the advances being the line that closes the reconciliation to the LK's balance sheet [S6] - which means growth consumes cash: FY2026E FCFF of US$-17.0m is depressed by the working-capital build as well as by capex. As growth slows the drag disappears and FCFF rises to US$521.3m by FY2030E. No release of the receivables balance is assumed anywhere in the base case - a receivable book at roughly half of sales is a risk, not an asset.

**Balance sheet and debt.** Net debt was US$1,345.5m at FY2025A, and the company repaid a maturing bond and sukuk issue in full and on schedule in August 2026 [S9]. Debt is predominantly USD-denominated while a large part of the cost base is rupiah, which is why the P&L carries large FX swings - a sizeable translation gain in FY2024 and a larger one in Q2-2026 [S0]. The company is naturally hedged on the revenue side (dollar exports) but not on the cost side. We set interest expense at US$306.9m, a cost of debt of 6.5% on opening debt, and hold debt flat; we do not capitalise FX gains, so other non-operating income is zero in the forecast. That is why FY2026E net profit (US$351.2m) is *below* FY2025A (US$453.3m): we have removed a non-recurring translation gain from the base year, not cut the business.

**Capital allocation.** Capex 25.1% of sales in FY2025A, 17.0% in FY2026E, 10.0% from FY2028E. Payout is a token 5.0% of earnings - the company retains cash for capacity, which is defensible at this valuation and also the reason the shares have no dividend floor [S0].

**Earnings quality, per the house screen.** Accruals: net profit less operating cash flow over average assets was negative in FY2025A, so earnings did not outrun cash - the problem is the opposite, that cash is tied up in receivables and fixed assets. Divergence flags: receivables at roughly half of annual sales, and inventory modest. IDX regime flags: none found - INKP is not on the special-monitoring board and carries no special notation in the house konglo registry (as of 27 October 2026). Related-party gravity: the parent and sister companies are the logical counterparties for a large share of sales, the modal value-destruction channel on IDX. The LK quantifies the receivable side even though it does not split sales: related-party trade receivables were US$1,328.8m at 30 June 2025 against US$452.3m from third parties [S6], about three-quarters of the book, and the related-party payable counterparties are listed in the bond prospectus [S7]. We model a quarter of that book never being collected in the bear case rather than in the base, because no impairment has been disclosed. Structure flags: none found beyond the ownership concentration itself - no rights issue in the period, no discounted private placement, no change of auditor noted.

We value INKP as a commodity producer with a finite, long-lived asset base: a ten-year explicit DCF of the free cash flow to the firm. We do not weight a multiple, and the choice is a source decision rather than a preference. The data pack's EBITDA is unusable (previous section), so an EV/EBITDA leg would apply a peer multiple to a number the LK contradicts; and the book value carries PSAK 16 revaluation gains that we cannot strip, so a peer P/BV leg would value a book we cannot verify. A method whose inputs are wrong does not enter the blend at a reduced weight - it leaves, and the report says so rather than presenting a cross-check we do not believe. The horizon stops at FY2035E because a paper machine's remaining economic life is finite and a terminal value beyond it would assume perpetual reinvestment into a mature market; terminal growth of 2.0% is below Indonesian nominal GDP because the company sells into global board markets.

The cost of capital is built from a risk-free rate of 5.0%, an equity risk premium of 4.2% plus a country risk premium of 2.5%, and a levered beta of 2.3x at the engine's 2.0x debt-to-equity. Those inputs are not all judgement: the house beta file has no PULP_PAPER industry regression, so the unlevered beta of 0.9x is the config default, and the debt-to-equity of 2.0x is gross debt over market capitalisation, capped by the engine at that level. The gross measure overstates economic leverage at a company whose cash covers most of its debt: on net debt the market D/E is far lower, and a beta a third higher than the config default relevered on net debt still gives a lower cost of equity than the 20.4% we use. So the cost of equity is not understated - but it is a house default, not a claim about this company. With pre-tax debt at 7.0% and a 22.0% tax shield, WACC is 10.4%.

The DCF gives an enterprise value of US$5,577.4m, of which the terminal value is 48.5% - a normal share for a ten-year horizon on long-lived assets, not a terminal-value story. After net debt that is Rp14,623 a share. The value is driven by three modelled facts and no others: the gross margin returning to 31.0% (below the FY2025A actual), capex falling to 10.0% of sales (from 25.1%), and working capital staying at 71.0% of sales without a single dollar released. The tax line is not flattered: the explicit years carry the rate the LK pays with the fourth mill's holiday, and the terminal year reverts to the FY2024 effective rate, so no perpetual holiday is capitalised.

The cross-checks we removed were not neutral. On the pack's FY2025A EBITDA the stock trades at 4.9x - a trough multiple on an understated metric; on the LK's implied EBITDA it trades lower still, so a peer-median EV/EBITDA leg applied to the pack number would have overstated the blend while looking like an independent check. The book-value leg had the opposite problem: 0.3x is the market's own multiple on a book that contains PSAK 16 revaluation gains, and a peer median above book applied to that book was a revaluation on a revaluation. We would rather own a single method we can rebuild from the LK than a blend whose two non-primary legs both rest on numbers the LK contradicts.

**Macro and FX.** The house macro regime is balance-of-payments pressure with a cautious tilt and a neutral reading on the commodity bloc, which is the regime this name sits in: dollar revenue, rupiah costs, and a current-account channel that moves the exchange rate more than it moves the mill. We convert the USD value per share at the spot rate the engine uses, 18,012, not the house deck's FY2027E rate of 18,350; using the deck rate would raise the IDR target, so our choice is the more conservative of the two and we say so rather than blend the two rates. The house deck's real GDP growth of 5.3% underpins the terminal growth rate, not the price forecast.

**What the price does and does not tell us.** At Rp6,425 the market capitalises IDR35,151.1bn. The engine's reverse DCF does not bracket the price, so we do not claim what the price implies about margins or capex.

**The konglo lens.** INKP is a Sinar Mas name: 58.3% held by APP Purinusa Ekapersada, the Widjaja family behind it, and a market that has spent 2026 de-rating exactly this kind of structure [S5]. The house konglo registry (as of 27 October 2026) classifies it as a Sinar Mas group name, records no high-concentration-list membership, no index deletion, no enforcement action and a free float of 39.7%; those are registry facts, not annual-report facts. The lens is the honest way to handle the ownership discount. Fundamental value today is Rp14,704, of which the price is 43.7%; the twelve-month fundamental value is Rp17,645. The lens does not assume the discount vanishes: the base regime scenario closes 30.0% of the log gap and keeps the rest, giving Rp9,884; the bear regime scenario assumes the discount widens further (Rp6,810); the bull scenario closes most of it (Rp13,765). The probability-weighted result is our Rp10,086 target. Why the base case closes only part of it: the mechanical pressures that hit the worst konglo names - high-concentration status, a float below the minimum, an index deletion, an enforcement action - do not apply here (house konglo registry, as of 27 October 2026). What remains is the general de-rating of family-controlled Indonesian assets, a sentiment variable with a date on it: the MSCI Standalone consultation takes feedback until April 2027 and a decision is due by June 2027. A positive outcome would be the largest single re-rating catalyst this name has.
**Scenario table.**

The business scenarios are mirrored on the two operating drivers: bear and bull move revenue growth and gross margin by the same amount in opposite directions, with base at fifty per cent. The other two shocks are deliberately asymmetric and the asymmetry is sourced: the bear carries a quarter of the related-party receivable book as never collected (working capital up ten points of sales) because no impairment is disclosed but the concentration is real [S6], and holds capex four points above plan because a competitive mill needs another line; the bull releases two points of working capital and saves two points of capex on the Karawang completion. Bear: 25.0% weight, Rp6,660. Base: Rp17,547. Bull: 25.0%, Rp28,827. The bull is the company's own four-year average margin, not the FY2022 pulp spike; we do not add a separate multiple re-rating to it, because the konglo bull regime scenario already prices the re-rating channel and adding it inside the operating bull would double-count the same move. The asymmetry in the outcomes comes from the operating leverage of a capital-intensive mill, not from asymmetric operating assumptions. If the bear carried half the probability weight, the weighted-in value would sit close to today's share price and the rating would be HOLD rather than BUY: the base case has to be the more likely path for the recommendation to stand.

**Downside risks, likelihood × impact.** *Commodity* - high likelihood, high impact: global board and pulp capacity additions keep the margin at the 2026 trough for longer than a year; the bear takes the margin to the Q3-2026 trough and leaves the equity barely above today's price, so the downside is real and not a modelling artefact. *Cash cycle and related parties* - medium likelihood, high impact: the related-party book is about three-quarters of trade receivables [S6]; a quarter of it never collected raises working capital permanently and is the bear's second-largest driver. *Execution* - medium, medium: Karawang's startup costs persist and the mill runs below nameplate, which is what the last two quarters show; the model already assumes a lower margin than FY2025A delivered [S0]. *FX and rates* - medium, medium: dollar debt against rupiah costs; a rupiah depreciation raises the cost base faster than dollar export prices, and the FX gain that flattered the first half of FY2026 reverses. *Capex* - medium, high: capex staying near the FY2025A peak for another cycle is in the bear and removes most of the free-cash-flow thesis. *Governance* - low-to-medium likelihood, high impact: the controller can direct asset purchases, related-party sales terms or a rights issue; there is no evidence of one in the period, but the structure permits it [S5]. *Regulatory and ESG* - medium, medium: forestry compliance and the group's fibre sourcing are the industry's permanent reputational exposure, and a licence or certification problem at Perawang would hit volume directly [S2]. *Liquidity* - low: average daily traded value is IDR37.7bn, enough to build a position, not enough for a quick exit in a panic.

**The konglo regime, separately.** The regime scenarios are not business scenarios and we treat them as such. The discount is a function of flows, not of the mill: MSCI's Standalone consultation, the exchange's free-float deadlines, and OJK's enforcement record against other Sinar Mas and Prajogo-linked names. INKP is a comparatively clean case - not on the high-concentration list, compliant float, no enforcement - which is why the base regime closes 30.0% of the log gap rather than all of it (house konglo registry, as of 27 October 2026). But we would be wrong to pretend we can time the turn: the bear regime scenario (Rp6,810) is a market-wide de-rating in which nothing about INKP's assets changes.

**Signposts that would change the view.** Gross margin below thirty per cent for two consecutive quarters; capex guidance above 17.0% of sales for FY2027; any related-party transaction above a tenth of assets; a dividend cut, or conversely a step-up in payout; and the MSCI decision in mid-2027.

**Ownership and control.** PT APP Purinusa Ekapersada holds 58.3% [S5]; the public holds 41.7%, with the exchange registry counting 39.7% as free float. The controlling shareholder is the Widjaja family's Sinar Mas group, and INKP's role in it is the industrial pulp and paper arm - the listed sister is Tjiwi Kimia [S4]. No pledged-share disclosure was available in the documents we retrieved; that is an open item, not a clean bill of health. On regime status the house konglo registry, as of 27 October 2026, records no high-shareholding-concentration listing, no index deletion, no enforcement action, and a free float of 39.7% above the minimum; those are registry readings, not annual-report ones, and the regime's own calendar sits in the valuation section.

**Related parties.** The group structure makes the parent and affiliates natural counterparties for fibre, energy, logistics and sales [S5]. The receivable side is quantified: related-party trade receivables were US$1,328.8m at 30 June 2025 against US$452.3m from third parties, about three-quarters of the book [S6], and the bond prospectus lists the related-party payable counterparties [S7]. The LK does not split sales by counterparty, so we do not claim a related-party revenue share; we model the concentration as a quarter loss of the receivable book in the bear, not in the base, because no impairment is disclosed. A reader should treat the unquantified sales split as the largest remaining governance gap in this report.

**Auditor and board.** The auditor's opinion and the board composition were not available in the documents we could retrieve; the president director is Hendra Jaya Kosasih and the corporate secretary Heri Santoso [S0]. We flag the gap rather than fill it.

**Dividends.** A token distribution: 5.0% of earnings in FY2025A, and a similar token amount in each of the four prior years [S0]. The cash is retained inside the group's industrial expansion, which is defensible at this valuation but means the shares offer no income support.

**ESG.** The material exposures are forestry and land use (the group's fibre supply and its conservation commitments), energy and emissions (captive coal-fired power at the mills), water, and community land disputes. The parent publishes a sustainability report and a forest conservation policy; the group's certification status is the single most consequential ESG fact for the export franchise, and we did not verify the current status mill by mill in this initiation - we say so rather than assert it [S4].

Dated catalysts: the FY2026 audited results in February 2027, the first full year with Karawang and the tax holiday in the tax line [S8]; the IDX free-float deadlines from March 2027, which INKP already clears; the MSCI Standalone decision by June 2027 (index calendar, not an annual-report fact); and each quarterly print in between, because the gross margin is the only variable that matters.

KPIs we watch, in order: gross margin per quarter (the ramp); capex as a percentage of sales (the end of the build); the receivables balance and its growth against revenue (the related-party channel); net debt and the bond maturity schedule [S9]; and any change in payout, because a step-up would signal that the group no longer needs the cash.

Market convention on IDX pulp and paper names has been to value them on price-to-book during downcycles and on EV/EBITDA during upcycles; neither is a through-cycle measure, which is why the same asset base can trade at a quarter of book in one year and two times book two years later. The 2026 market-wide de-rating of family-controlled conglomerate vehicles has compressed that range further than the operating cycle alone would justify.

bear.narrative: Board and pulp prices stay at the 2026 trough while Karawang startup costs persist: gross margin falls to the Q3-2026 trough level, growth stalls, a quarter of the related-party receivable book is never collected (working capital rises permanently by 10pp of sales), and capex stays at 21% of sales because the mill needs another line to stay competitive.

bull.narrative: Pulp and containerboard prices recover through 2027 as Chinese demand and Indonesian supply discipline hold, Karawang ramps to plan, the margin returns to the four-year average, working capital releases 2pp and capex stays 2pp below plan.

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +11.1% is the actual 9M2026 run-rate (net sales US$2,626m vs US$2,363m, +11.1%), carried through Q4 with no deceleration assumed; then 3.0%, 3.0%, 2.5%, 2.0% volume-led with selling prices held flat in nominal terms after the 2022-25 pulp/board downcycle. No price spike is built in and no volume haircut is taken against the ramp the company is already running.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2025A delivered 32.2% and FY2024A 31.9% (LK [S3, S6]); 9M2026 fell to 30.5% as the Karawang mill ran pre-commercial startup costs while board prices stayed near the trough (Q3-2026 gross margin 28.3%). Base case 30.0% in FY2026E, then 31.0%/31.5% as Karawang ramps and the pulp cycle mean-reverts; never assumes a return to the 2021-22 peak (FY2022A gross margin 39.7%).

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: LK selling plus general and administrative expense US$365.7m on FY2024 net sales US$3,195.7m (11.4%), US$351.8m on FY2025 (11.1%); 9M2026 US$293.4m on US$2,626m (11.2%). Held at 11.1% flat, the last actual, with no efficiency credit.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The data pack's depreciation (US$7.5m FY2025) is a fraction of the charge: the issuer's own ratio table shows EBITDA/net sales of 29.30% FY2024 against operating margin 20.43%, implying D&A of US$283m (8.9% of sales), and 29.16% vs 22.64% in FY2023 (US$227m, 6.5%); machinery is depreciated over 25 years (4%) and buildings over 20 (5%) on a PPE base of US$5.8bn (LK [S6, S7]). Modelled at 7.8% of revenue, the mid-point of the FY2023-24 disclosed range.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2024A 40.1% and FY2025A 25.1% of sales were the Karawang containerboard build; 9M2026 capex US$417m (15.9%) shows the spend already normalising. Base case 17% FY2026E (completion), 12% FY2027E, then 10% - about US$340m, 1.35x D&A, a normalised sustaining-plus-efficiency level for a 25-year-life asset base; no growth project beyond Karawang is credited.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025A operating working capital US$2,256m on sales US$3,171m (71.1%): trade receivables US$1,530m plus inventory US$415m plus advances US$665m less trade payables US$354m. The advances are the line the prior text omitted - S6 shows uang muka of US$752m at Dec-2024 and US$690m at Jun-2025, so US$665m at Dec-2025 is the balancing item. Held at 71%, the last actual - no working-capital release is assumed.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025A tax US$94.6m on pre-tax profit US$547.9m (17.3%); FY2024A 19.5% (LK). The 17% reflects the mill-specific, time-limited tax holiday on the fourth mill [S8] plus ordinary permanent differences, not a group rate in perpetuity: the explicit years stay at 17% and the terminal year reverts to the 19.5% the LK paid in FY2024, before the holiday's full-year benefit.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2024A interest expense US$300.9m on opening debt US$3,456m = 8.7%; FY2025A US$303.0m on US$4,637m = 6.5% as the USD bonds were refinanced. Set at 6.5%, the current coupon level on a debt stack that is predominantly USD bonds.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025A interest income US$59.0m on opening cash US$3,113m = 1.9%; set at 1.9% consistent with USD deposits.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Debt held flat: FY2026E free cash flow after capex covers the small dividend and the USD bonds maturing are refinanced, as the issuer has done each year since 2020 (bond/sukuk programme disclosed in [S6]).

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Set to zero: FY2024A-9M2026 non-operating lines are dominated by FX gains on USD cash and IDR liabilities (US$78m in FY2024, US$157m in Q2-2026 alone) which are a translation effect, not a recurring cash engine, so the base case does not capitalise them.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minority interests are US$0.46m on the balance sheet and the minority share of net profit is nil to negative in FY2023A-FY2025A (LK); set to zero.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 earnings paid Rp75/share (Rp410bn, about US$25m) = 5.5% of net profit; the prior four years paid Rp50 (about 4%). A Sinar Mas vehicle retaining cash for the pulp/board expansion, so 5% is the policy, not a temporary trough - it is the group's stated allocation [S5].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No share issuance assumed: 5,470.98m shares outstanding unchanged since 2019 and no rights issue announced [S5].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2.0% nominal: Indonesian pulp and paper demand grows with GDP (real 5.3% house deck) but the company exports into a mature global board market and the mill base cannot expand without new fibre supply.

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA leg (20% weight) applies 7.555x to metric 675.2 - the pack's FY2025A EBITDA that the report itself calls understated by an order of magnitude and says it does not use 'for anything'. On the LK's own 29.30% FY2024 EBITDA margin applied to FY2025 sales the metric is US$929.2m, giving about Rp19,373 a share, not Rp13,055. Section 4 also calls this the 'FY2026E trough year' when the metric is FY2025A. Correcting only this leg lifts the blend to about Rp17,300 and the target to about Rp11,180.
challenges.answer: The EV/EBITDA leg is removed rather than re-run on the pack metric: FY2025A EBITDA of US$675m is contradicted by the LK ratio table and by S7 note 14, so no multiple now touches it. Section 4 states the metric period and withdraws the 'used for nothing' sentence. [S7][S6][S0]

challenges.challenge: The model mixes two D&A bases: history carries pack D&A of US$7.5m (FY2025A) and US$11.5m (FY2024A) while forecasts carry 7.8% of sales (US$268.4m). FY2025A EBITDA in the model is therefore 675.2 / 21.3% while the analyst's own restatement makes it 929.2 / 29.3%. The method card requires the line to be restated as sourced facts, not explained in qc_justifications, and this inconsistency is what feeds C1. S7 note 14 gives audited total depreciation of US$252.891m for FY2022 and US$57.132m for Q1-2023; S6 gives the ratio table.
challenges.answer: Added F18, audited FY2022 total depreciation of US$252.9m from S7 note 14; FY2023-FY2025 audited cash-flow statements are not in the archive, so no fact was invented. The work changed instead: both multiple legs dropped, so no valuation line now uses the pack's D&A history, and section 3 states the limitation openly. [S7][S6]

challenges.challenge: The bear uses two shocks (growth -3pp, gross margin -2pp) and still values the equity at Rp16,747, so no modelled path goes below 2.6x the price. The risks the report itself lists are absent: the US$1,328.8m related-party receivable book (74.6% of trade receivables at 30 Jun 2025, S6), a reversal of the US$157m Q2-2026 FX gain, capex staying near 25% of sales, and Q3-2026's 28.3% gross margin persisting. The scenario set cannot express the thesis' failure mode, so the section 5 claim that the bear 'still values the equity above today's price' is a conclusion the design guarantees rather than tests.
challenges.answer: Bear rebuilt with four sourced shocks: growth -3pp, gross margin -3pp to the Q3-2026 trough, working capital +10pp (a quarter of the US$1,328.8m related-party book) and capex +4pp. Bear target is Rp6,650 against a Rp6,425 price; at half weight the target would be near the price, a HOLD. [S6][S0]

challenges.challenge: Bull moves gross margin to 32% when FY2022A delivered 39.7% (S7: 1,589.939/4,002.632) and FY2023A 32.5% - the bull reaches less than the four-year average amplitude, and no scenario models a pulp or containerboard price recovery at all (prices held flat in nominal terms to FY2035). The upside case is compressed to Rp22,463, only 16.6% above base.
challenges.answer: Bull gross margin raised to 34.5%, the FY2022-FY2025 average (FY2022A 39.7%, FY2023A 32.5%, FY2024A 31.9%, FY2025A 32.2%). No pulp or containerboard price series is archived, so the amplitude is calibrated on the realised margin rather than a fabricated index. [S7][S6][S0]

challenges.challenge: No scenario or cross-check carries the re-rating channel, yet 20% of the blend is a multiple and the stock trades at 3.8x pack / about 5.9x restated EV/EBITDA against the 7.56x peer median the report itself uses. A bull in which the market applies the peer median to restated EBITDA is the largest single upside lever in the model and is nowhere tested; the bull only moves operating assumptions.
challenges.answer: The re-rating channel is priced through the konglo bull regime scenario, which closes most of the log gap and is already in the probability-weighted target; adding a peer-median multiple to the operating bull would double-count the same move. Section 5 states the exclusion and its value. [S0]

challenges.challenge: Sections 3 and 6 say the related-party share of revenue 'could not be quantified from the retrieved documents'. The analyst's own S6 shows related-party trade receivables of US$1,328.8m against third-party US$452.3m at 30 Jun 2025 (1,355.4m vs 488.2m at 31 Dec 2024), i.e. 74.6% of the book, and S7 lists the related-party payable counterparties. The report calls receivables at half of sales 'a risk, not an asset' but never quantifies counterparty concentration or tests a haircut.
challenges.answer: Related-party trade receivables quantified at US$1,328.8m of a US$1,781.1m book (74.6%) at 30 Jun 2025 via facts F19 and F20; the bear treats a quarter of that book as permanently uncollected. Related-party sales are not disclosed in S6 or S7. [S6][S7]

challenges.challenge: The P/BV leg applies the 1.07x peer median to book equity of US$7,279.4m (Rp23,966 a share) even though the report's own DCF uses COE 20.41% and S3 shows FY2025A ROE of 6.6% (453.3/6,843.8). A justified P/BV on those inputs is (0.066-0.02)/(0.2041-0.02) = 0.25x, roughly the 0.27x the market pays, not 1.07x. The leg is +74% versus the DCF and contributes about Rp1,440 a share to the blend; section 4 both calls book 'a floor indicator, not a valuation' and weights it 15%. The PSAK 16 revaluation is asserted, not evidenced or stripped.
challenges.answer: The P/BV leg is dropped rather than re-based: the PSAK 16 revaluation is asserted and not evidenced, and a justified P/BV on COE 20.4% and ROE 6.6% is about 0.25x. The DCF is now the only method, at weight 1.0. [S3][S0]

challenges.challenge: Every cost-of-capital input is an engine default, not an analyst choice: beta_unlevered 0.9 'industry default (config)', D/E 2.0, ERP 4.23%, CRP 2.46%, rf 4.99%. Section 4 presents them as judgement ('we set... a levered beta of 2.3x at the house's 2.0x debt-to-equity') and asserts 'a WACC in this range is, if anything, conservative'. The company's market D/E is 0.59x (net debt 1,149.1 / market cap 1,951.5) and book D/E 0.16x, so 2.0x is 3.4x actual market leverage, and a 0.9 unlevered beta is at the low end for a pulp and paper cyclical.
challenges.answer: The engine's D/E is gross debt over market cap (US$5,311.7m / US$1,951.5m = 2.72x, capped at 2.0), not the 0.59x net figure; the house beta file has no PULP_PAPER regression and no INKP ticker, so 0.9 is the config default, not an analyst pick. A beta a third higher relevered on net debt still gives a lower COE than the 20.4% used, and the 'conservative' label is withdrawn. [S0]

challenges.challenge: Two unsourced conservatism items in the drivers: (a) FY2026E revenue growth of 8.5% is described as the run-rate but the 9M2026 run-rate is +11.1% (2,626 vs 2,363), so Q4-2026 must grow only +0.9% - roughly US$80m of revenue left out with no stated reason; (b) the nwc_pct 71.1% basis reads 'receivables 1,530 + inventory 415 less payables 354', which is 1,591, not the 2,256 modelled (a US$665m, 21pp gap), so the driver cannot be verified from the text.
challenges.answer: FY2026E growth is now the actual 9M2026 run-rate of +11.1% (US$2,626m vs US$2,363m), carried through Q4 with no deceleration; the NWC basis includes the advances line, so 1,530 + 415 + 665 - 354 = US$2,256m, 71.1% of sales. [S0][S6]

challenges.challenge: Optimism in the tax line: 17.0% is applied to all group profit for ten years plus terminal, while the only cited support is a 20-year holiday on the fourth mill reported by a broker-sourced news story (S8, Investor.id 8 Sep 2026) and FY2024A's effective rate was 19.5% (S6). The report also asserts the holiday explains why the effective rate sits below statutory without quantifying the holiday's share of profit. A mill-specific, time-limited holiday cannot support a group-wide rate in perpetuity.
challenges.answer: The 17% is kept only for the explicit years where the mill-specific holiday applies, with the terminal rate reverted to the FY2024 effective 19.5%; section 2 now says the holiday is a partial, time-limited explanation, not a group rate in perpetuity. [S6][S8]

challenges.challenge: The commodity-cyclical card requires a sourced through-cycle price (10y real average or incentive price), NAV at spot versus through-cycle, and a cost-curve quartile. The report has none: it holds selling prices flat in nominal terms to FY2035 with no named pulp or containerboard series, gives no cost-curve position, and does not carry the house macro regime (balance_of_payments_pressure / CAUTIOUS) or the commodity-bloc NEUTRAL tilt. It also converts the USD value at spot 18,012 rather than the house deck's 18,350, which by itself understates the IDR target by about 1.9%.
challenges.answer: Section 2 now names the through-cycle anchor (the realised gross margin, base below the FY2022-FY2025 range, bull at the four-year average), shows NAV at spot and through-cycle, states that no cost-curve study is archived instead of inventing a quartile, and section 4 carries the balance_of_payments_pressure regime and the deck's USD/IDR path. [S2][S6][S0]

challenges.challenge: Sections 1 and 2 say Indonesia's pulp and paper industry 'exported US$8.2m in 2025'; the cited S2 says 'US$8,2 miliar', i.e. US$8.2 billion (F15 stores 8.2 USD bn). A thousand-fold unit error, repeated, in the industry-size paragraph. Section 3 also writes 'a cost of debt of 306.9' (that is interest expense in US$m) and 'hold that ratio at 2,443.0 of sales' (that is NWC in US$m; the ratio is 71.1%), and section 4 writes 'IDR35,151,065,395.93tn' and ADTV 'IDR37,716,380,238.1bn'.
challenges.answer: Units corrected throughout: exports read US$8.2 billion via F15, interest expense and working capital are placeholders with the ratio stated, market capitalisation is in IDR bn and ADTV in IDR bn. [S2][S0]

challenges.challenge: The discount is stated inconsistently and the target mechanism is inverted. Section 4 says 'the price is 39.7% of it' with fundamental Rp19,432 (6,425/19,432 = 33.1%; 39.7% is price/Rp16,185), then says 'a discount of roughly two-thirds'. It also says 'the base regime scenario keeps 30.0% of the gap and closes the rest' when fund record closes 30% and keeps 70% (premium_kept 0.5238, Rp10,178); section 1 has it the right way round. Separately, the konglo registry facts (39.66% float, no HSC, no index deletion, no enforcement) are cited to S5, which is the AR ownership table showing 58.31/41.69% and none of those items; the lens sources them to its own S3/S25.
challenges.answer: One discount definition is kept: the price as a share of fundamental twelve-month value, with the base regime closing the stated share of the log gap. Konglo float and regime facts now cite the house konglo registry as of 27 October 2026, not S5. [S5][S0]

challenges.challenge: post_bs_review claims a search 'since the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet' and a 'USD 7.31m principal repaid July 2026', citing S6 - a bond/sukuk summary dated September 2025 whose latest balance sheet is 30 June 2025, which can attest neither. The 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet that supplies the whole bridge (cash 4,162.6, debt 5,311.7, net debt 1,149.1) is not in any archived source. S9 separately documents a Rp2.49tn repayment on 26 Aug 2026, closer to what matters.
challenges.answer: post_bs_review now cites the 30 Sep 2026 data pack for cash US$4,162.6m, debt US$5,311.7m and net debt US$1,149.1m, and S9 for the Rp2.49tn repayment on 26 August 2026, which sits inside that debt; the USD 7.31m July amortisation is identified as a separate item. [S0][S9]

challenges.challenge: The engine's reverse DCF returns available false, 'price not bracketed', yet section 4 asserts what the price implies (gross margin never recovering above FY2026E and capex staying at the FY2025A peak for the life of the assets) and the extreme_call justification repeats it as the answer to 'what today's price implies'. No computed reverse DCF supports the sentence.
challenges.answer: The reverse-DCF claim is deleted from section 4 and the extreme_call justification now states that the reverse DCF does not bracket the price, so no implied-margin or implied-capex sentence remains. [S0]

challenges.challenge: QC round 2 Q6 is not fixed: summary paragraph 2 still says the business earned an EBITDA margin of 29.3 percent of sales in FY2024 and a similar figure in FY2025, while the engine FY2025A EBITDA is USD675.2m / 21.3 percent and section 3 states FY2025A was NOT restated and stays on the pack basis. The first variant pillar therefore rests on a margin the model does not carry.
challenges.answer: Investment summary now states FY2024 EBITDA margin of {{fact.F8|pct}} restated from the LK and FY2025A of {{fin.FY2025A.ebitda_margin|pct}} on the data pack basis, flagged as the one unrestated year; no longer implies an LK-level FY2025A margin [S6][S7].

missing_bull_case.note: Bull moves gross margin only +2pp to 32% and growth +3pp; FY2022A gross margin was 39.7% (S7, 1,589.9/4,002.6), so the scenario set is calibrated at a third of the company's own four-year amplitude. No scenario carries a multiple re-rating channel either, although 20% of the blend is a multiple and the stock trades at 3.8x pack / about 5.9x restated EV/EBITDA against the 7.56x peer median the report uses.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear (GM 28%, growth 5.5%) values the equity at Rp16,747, 2.6x the price: a worst case that cannot lose money. None of the risks enumerated in section 5 is in any scenario - related-party receivables of US$1,328.8m out of US$1,781.1m total at 30 Jun 2025 (S6), the US$157m Q2-2026 FX gain reversing, capex overrun at Karawang, or Q3-2026's 28.3% gross margin persisting.

assumption_realism.note: Most drivers are anchored and defensible: GM 30.0% is below the FY2025A 32.2% actual, capex normalisation is sourced to 9M2026 15.9%, opex held at 11.1%, FX gains not capitalised, no working-capital release. Two do not hold: FY2026E revenue growth of 8.5% is below the 9M2026 run-rate of +11.1% (2,626/2,363) and implies Q4-2026 growth of +0.9%, unsourced; and the nwc_pct 71% basis (2,256 = 1,530 + 415 - 354) does not arithmetically add, missing about US$665m.

evidence_and_citations.note: Load-bearing items verified correctly: S5 58.31/41.69 ownership, S3 FY2025 gross margin 32.2% and ROE 6.6%, S6 ratio-table column order FY2024/FY2023, S7 FY2022 gross margin 39.7% and total depreciation US$252.891m, S9 Rp2.49tn repayment 26 Aug 2026, S8 20-year tax holiday. But S2 says US$8.2bn and the report writes US$8.2m twice; the konglo registry facts (39.66% float, no HSC, no enforcement) are cited to S5, which contains none of them; post_bs_review cites S6 for July 2026 events; fund record labels fractions as pct.

valuation_method_fit.note: The DCF itself is sound: EV US$5,613.7m is 6.1x restated FY2026E EBITDA, terminal value 48.9%, the bridge ties to the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet, and the FCFF arithmetic reconciles (FY2035E 562.1). The cross-checks do not: EV/EBITDA applies 7.56x to the un-restated US$675.2m, and P/BV applies 1.07x when the report's own COE 20.4% and ROE 6.6% justify 0.25x. Both divergences are explained with narratives that contradict the arithmetic.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose overshoots its own numbers three times: price is 33.1% of Rp19,432 (not 39.7%, which is price/Rp16,185); the EV at Rp6,425 is 55% of the DCF EV (not 'roughly a third'); and section 4 says the base 'keeps 30% of the gap and closes the rest' when the engine keeps 70%. The BUY survives the bear probability doubled (about 18,800), but only because the bear is mild.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The commodity-cyclical card requires a named through-cycle price series and NAV at spot vs through-cycle, a cost-curve position, and the complex/macro tilt. The report has none: selling prices are held flat in nominal terms to FY2035 with no source, no cost-curve quartile, and no reference to the house balance_of_payments_pressure regime or commodity-bloc NEUTRAL tilt. IDR conversion uses spot 18,012 rather than the deck's 18,350.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservatism stack: revenue 8.5% vs 11.1% run-rate; no working-capital release though FY2024-FY2025 released US$443m; GM 30.0% vs 30.5% in 9M2026; capex held at 17% in FY2026E; spot FX. Each is small, together worth roughly 2-4% of value. Offset by one optimism: a 17.0% tax rate on all group profit through terminal on a mill-specific, news-sourced 20-year holiday (FY2024A was 19.5%).

calibration.note: All three BLOCK flags are marked justified but the calibration justification is not implemented: model D&A is 7.5 in FY2025A and 268.4 in FY2026E, so FY2025A EBITDA stays at 675.2 / 21.3% against the analyst's own restated 29-30%. The method card says restate the line, not justify the drift. The extreme_call justification also relies on a reverse DCF the engine reports as price not bracketed.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. BUY, target Rp10,086 (price Rp6,425, +57.9%). Read with TKIM as one industry judgement: both Sinar Mas names are outside the HSC list, floats 39.7%/29.2% clear the 15% minimum, and both BUYs rest on the same house konglo lens (base closes 30% of the log gap) applied to genuinely cheap fundamentals, not on a shared input error. INKP: 100% DCF is right because the pack EBITDA is unusable and the PSAK 16 book cannot be stripped; fundamental value Rp14,623 today and Rp17,645 in twelve months, premium kept 57.2%. Base gross margin 30.0-31.5% sits below FY2025A 32.2% and below the FY2022-25 average, anchored on the 9M2026 30.5% run-rate (Q3 28.3% on Karawang startup), so the base is the most likely path, not a safety haircut; capex normalisation 25.1% to 10.0% is sourced to Karawang completion; FX at spot 18,012 is the disclosed conservative choice. Related-party receivables are quantified (74.6% of the book at 30 Jun 2025) and the bear haircuts a quarter; the konglo profile cites the registry as of 2026-10-27. Residual, not material to the call: Q11 (summary para 1 still says the margin of the last actual year while section 3 uses 30.0% vs 32.2%) and notes Q8/Q10/Q12 to correct at the next update.

bias.note: Base gross margin 31.5pct terminal sits 0.7pp below FY2025A 32.2pct and below the FY2022-25 average 34.1pct on a mix-shift rationale, mildly conservative, offset by sourced capex normalisation to 10pct and 17pct explicit tax. Scenarios mirror growth and gross margin at plus or minus 3pp; capex and NWC asymmetries sourced to S0/S6. No unsourced optimism. Model FY2026E net debt of 1,586.6 runs 437m above the actual 30 Sep 2026 net debt of 1,149.1, a conservative cash-flow assumption that does not affect the bridge (S0).

recomputed.item: FY2024A D&A (29.30pct x sales less EBIT)
Related-party share of trade receivables 30 Jun 2025

findings.finding: Summary para 1 still says the mills are worth at the margin the last actual year actually earned. The engine FY2026E EBITDA margin is 26.7pct (base gross margin 30.0-31.5pct) against a restated FY2025A of about 29.5pct and FY2025A gross margin of 32.2pct, so the DCF is not at the last actual year margin. The para-2 basis is correctly fixed (29.3pct FY2024 restated / 21.3pct FY2025A pack) but the prior Q6 para-1 element remains unapplied (S6).
Section 2 says the bull lifts gross margin to the FY2022-25 average; that average is 34.1pct while the bull terminal margin is 34.5pct.

WACC uses 7.0pct pre-tax debt vs cost_of_debt 6.5pct; forecast D&A is 7.8pct of sales vs the 8.9pct FY2024 implied; COE applies the levered beta to ERP plus CRP. All three overstate cost of capital and understate EBITDA and are conservative, not a valuation error.

The model FY2026E net-debt line of 1,586.6 is 437m above the actual 30 Sep 2026 net debt of 1,149.1, implying cash burn while net debt actually fell 196m in 9M2026. The DCF bridge correctly uses the actual 1,149.1 and the target is unaffected, but the forecast FCFF and net-debt trajectory should be reconciled.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +5.4pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: The +5.4pp gap is a data restatement, not a forecast improvement. The pack's D&A is US$7.5m against an audited FY2022 charge of US$252.9m [S7 note 14] and an LK ratio table showing EBITDA/net sales of 29.30% in FY2024 and 29.16% in FY2023 against operating margins of 20.4% and 22.6% [S6]; machinery is depreciated over 25 years on a PPE base of US$5.8bn. FY2026E EBITDA margin of 26.7% is therefore BELOW the FY2023-24 actuals. No multiple leg now uses the understated pack history.

flags.message: a.capex_pct moves -7.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Capex falls from 17.0% of sales in FY2026E to 10.0% from FY2028E because the Karawang containerboard mill completes: FY2024A ran 40.1% and FY2025A 25.1% of sales on that build, while the first nine months of 2026 are already at 15.9% [S0][S6]. 10% of sales is about 1.35x D&A, a normalised sustaining-plus-efficiency level for a 25-year asset base, and no new growth project is credited.

flags.message: a.capex_pct: bear 0.04 vs bull -0.02 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The bear holds capex 4pp above plan because a competitive mill needs another line; the bull's 2pp saving is the completion of the Karawang build already in the model [S0][S6]. Mirroring the bear's +4pp would assume a new project in the bull, which is not the bull thesis.

flags.message: a.nwc_pct: bear 0.1 vs bull -0.02 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
